SMTO-EXE-0059 — The computer didn't let SMTO see or stop that program

GUID: 200a8951-4bb2-5316-8921-99356ee43f30
Slug: desktop-process-access-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The operating system on the Gateway computer refused SMTO access to that program, usually because it belongs to another user or runs with administrator rights. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the program was started by the same user that the Gateway (SMTO's helper program) runs as on that computer. The system only lets the Gateway see and stop programs belonging to its own user.
  2. If the program runs as an administrator or another user, ask the person who manages that computer to handle it there directly. Programs with higher rights are off-limits to the Gateway by design.
  3. Otherwise, ask SMTO to list the running apps again and choose one of your own. A fresh list shows which programs SMTO is allowed to work with.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows details for the program you chose, or completes the action on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't run the Gateway as an administrator to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • psutil raised AccessDenied while the Gateway inspected, resolved or signalled the selected process under its own account.

What this means

  • The process API raised AccessDenied while inspecting, resolving or signaling the selected process under the Gateway account. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The process API raised AccessDenied while inspecting, resolving or signaling the selected process under the Gateway account.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether read access or signal access failed and inspect the current process owner and identity.

How to fix it

  • Use a process owned by the Gateway's session user and check the target's ownership, elevation or integrity level and any OS process-protection policy. The Gateway never elevates; processes that need higher rights must be handled outside this capability.
  • Use a process owned by the Gateway session user and inspect its current permissions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a process owned by the Gateway session user and inspect its current permissions.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported process is accessible under authorized permissions and its state is observed.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
